idiom_name: @Override delegating method (hand-written; IDE or annotation-processor generation as tooling)
implementation_notes: Java has no expression bodies, no delegation clause and no property syntax, so the one-line method is written in full - @Override public CancelResult cancel(OrderId id) { return repo.cancel(id); } - and HotSpot inlines it once the call site is warm. Tooling partially replaces the classic structure: IDEs generate forwarding blocks for a whole interface in one action, and Lombok's @Delegate copies every public method of a field, but Lombok's own documentation marks that feature experimental and negative and warns support may be dropped, so generated delegation stays a convenience rather than the load-bearing mechanism. Write the one-liner by hand where the method renames the operation or must own its documentation.
pitfalls: Lombok @Delegate copies every public method of the field, including the ones you did not want, and the feature is documented as experimental - a later JDK can break it, so keep generated delegation out of published APIs.
Forwarding methods inherit checked-exception signatures; a wrapper that narrows the throws clause silently drops a documented failure mode for its callers.
Object methods are excluded from generated delegation, so equals/hashCode are not forwarded and a wrapper never equals its delegate - collections and caches see two different objects.
